narrative:
The model determined that you have a 72.5% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your academic record. Your first-year and third-year class rankings were the strongest factors pushing the prediction toward failure. Both placed you in the bottom decile of your school, far below the average of roughly the sixth and fifth deciles among students who were admitted. These unusually low rankings signaled to the model a pattern of academic struggle that strongly suggested difficulty passing the bar.

Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor, but it worked in the opposite direction. At 3.20 it sits only slightly below the 3.23 average of accepted students, so the model viewed it as a modest positive that slightly increased the chance you might pass. Unfortunately, this small encouraging signal was not enough to outweigh the much larger negative impact of your class rankings.

The model did not consider your gender, race, family income bracket, LSAT score, or planned full-time status when making this prediction.

To improve your chances, focus on strengthening your academic performance and consider retaking courses or seeking additional bar-preparation support before reapplying. Raising your class standing in future semesters would have the biggest effect on future model assessments. (218 words)
